parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This file is an HTTP request-parsing adapter, and it sits in the infrastructure layer. Its job is to take untrusted, unknown-typed request bodies and query values and turn them into application command DTOs (PlaceOrderCommand) or a typed OrderState. When the input is malformed it throws ValidationError. Every check is about the shape or type of the incoming data: is it an object, is it a non-empty string, is it a non-empty array, is it a number. That is transport-level input validation, which belongs in infrastructure.

The file does not decide any business rules. For example, it checks that quantity is a number but does not check that it is positive or within limits; that is left to the application or domain layer. To decide whether an order state is valid, it calls the domain's isOrderState instead of keeping its own copy of the list of states. There is no persistence, orchestration or domain logic. All of its responsibilities fit the infrastructure layer.
